quotes.text: Productivity doesn't fail because people can't type fast enough. It fails because decisions get lost in the noise. Copilot's role is to keep those decisions surfaced where they can't slip away.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the real productivity problem Copilot in Teams is meant to solve.

quotes.text: Yes, Copilot uses similar underlying language models, but those models are grounded in your company's own environment. It isn't here to explain the universe. It's here to interpret your workstreams.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates Copilot's grounded, tenant-specific role from general chatbots.

quotes.text: The number one starting point is licensing. You can't get around it. To run Copilot inside teams, you need to already be on Microsoft three sixty five, E three or E five.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the first prerequisite most failed Copilot rollouts skip.

quotes.text: Copilot relies on transcription data to build these summaries and insights. If transcription is not turned on, you're going to get inconsistent or incomplete results.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains a concrete technical dependency admins often overlook.

quotes.text: The smart move is resisting the urge to treat Copilot as the final word. Its real strength is giving structured, actionable information faster than humans can on their own.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames Copilot as decision support rather than decision authority.

takeaways: Copilot in Teams only works when licensing, up-to-date clients, admin permissions and meeting transcription are all in place before launch.
Used during meetings with direct prompts, Copilot turns live conversations into structured summaries, action items and links to the relevant files.
Copilot should feed decisions and tools like Planner or Power BI, but people remain responsible for verifying commitments and making the final call.
hook: Teams holds your meetings, chats and files, yet decisions still get lost and people spend hours hunting for who committed to what. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins and team leads who want Copilot in Teams set up correctly, from licensing and transcription to pilot testing, and used to turn meetings into clear, actionable outcomes.
